newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH KGHM'S UNION GETS MEDIATOR IN WAGE DISPUTE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH KGHM'S UNION GETS MEDIATOR IN WAGE DISPUTE.

text.p: Poland's labour ministry appointed a mediator for KGHM copper concern's Solidarity union after it went on strike alert on Monday over the lack of a such a person in its wage dispute with the board, a union official said.
Jozef Czyczerski told Reuters however, the union would lift the strike alert only after the mediator sets the date for the start of negotiations with the board.
"The labour minister has appointed a mediator, as we have reqested for so long, but we will not lift the strike alert until the mediator sets a date for talks," Czyczerski said.
Solidarity demands a monthly rise of 150 zlotys or 7.5 percent of the average pay for the company's 27,000 workers employed directly in production.

Czyczerski said that once the starting date for negotiations is set, the dispute could be resolved in a matter of weeks. "The case is so clear, that in two weeks the problems should be solved," he said.

Solidarity also opposes the restructuring of the firm, under which a part of the workforce employed directly in production would be moved to KGHM's fully owned auxiliary firms or subsidiaries involved in services.

The second of KGHM's two biggest unions, the Union of Copper Industry Workers (ZZPPM), also demands wage increases, but only of 5.7 percent of the average wage in the company, now at 2,000 zlotys. The average wage in Poland is 948 zlotys.
KGHM's president has said the board would consider wage rises at the end of the year, once it has the company's financial results after the first three quarters.
But KGHM's spokesman has said that considering the current low prices of copper on world markets any wage rises this year were unlikely.

KGHM, one of the world's major copper and silver producers is slated for privatisation in the second quarter of 1997. The value of the concern, employing a total of 42,500, is estimated at $2-3 billion. Its shares are to be floated both on the international and domestic markets.
